notes_context:
These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0003] Raise BillingError with stable snake_case codes: Reject invalid billing input by raising BillingError(code, detail) from ledgerly.errors with the established codes such as "invalid_state", "invalid_quantity" and "negative_amount"; do not use ValueError or bare exceptions.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 3x, 1 passed, 1 failed)
- [at-0001] Round money only with round_money: Always round monetary Decimal results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 2x, 1 passed, 1 failed)
- [at-0004] Guard mutations on invoice draft status: Mutating operations on an Invoice must first check invoice.status != "draft" and raise BillingError("invalid_state", ...) with the invoice id and status, matching issue_invoice in ledgerly/invoice.py.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0005] Normalize datetimes with ensure_utc: In ledgerly, normalize every incoming datetime with `ensure_utc` from `ledgerly.clock` before comparing or doing arithmetic (see `current_period` in `ledgerly/subscriptions.py`).
  (learned from task E03 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 2x, 0 passed, 0 failed)

review_comments: [team convention] Money in ledgerly is Decimal end-to-end and always has exactly two decimal places. Never convert amounts to float.
